– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure is caused by a ZipException raised during the loading of a zip64 archive. The exception states that the central directory zip64 extended information extra field's length does not match the expected central directory data length. Examining the ZipFile class reveals that during reading of central directory entries (in method readCentralDirectoryEntry), the extra field from the central directory is read and then passed to setSizesAndOffsetFromZip64Extra. This method extracts the Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField, and then calls reparseCentralDirectoryData on it, passing booleans indicating which zip64 fields should be present based on magic values from the central directory entry.

The method Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField.reparseCentralDirectoryData computes the expected length of the rawCentralDirectoryData by summing DWORD (8 bytes) or WORD (2 bytes) length contributions depending on which fields are supposed to exist. If the actual length does not match this expected length, a ZipException is thrown, as is the case in the reported failure.

This implies that for some valid zip64 archives (such as those created by DotNetZip-WinFormsTool), the central directory extra field's length differs from the sum of the expected fields. The current code expects a strict match, which may not hold for all zip64 implementations and may cause this exception when opening zip64 archives with excess data in the extra fields.

This diagnosis matches the test method testExcessDataInZip64ExtraField, which appears designed to test loading zip files where the zip64 extra field has more data than minimal or expected, causing this specific failure.

Recent bug reports about other ZipFile reading issues (like duplicate entries) seem unrelated.

Thus, the bug occurs because the method reparseCentralDirectoryData enforces a strict length check on the zip64 extra field in central directory entries, rejecting valid zip64 archives that contain additional, unexpected data in these extra fields. The implementation needs to be tolerant of extra data beyond the required fields rather than strictly matching lengths.

This explains the root cause of ZipException for valid zip64 files with excess data in zip64 extended extra fields.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField.reparseCentralDirectoryData(boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
